def-bounded-lipschitz-dual-norm-for-sign:
## Definition

Let $\omega,
u$ be finite signed Borel measures on $\mathbb R^d$ such that $|\omega-
u|(\mathbb R^d)<\infty$. For each bounded Lipschitz test function, integration against $\omega-
u$ is defined by [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]; boundedness and finite total variation make every test in the following set integrable. Set $\|\phi\|_\infty:=\sup_x|\phi(x)|$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(\phi):=\sup_{x
e y}|\phi(x)-\phi(y)|/|x-y|$, using the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Define the bounded-Lipschitz dual discrepancy
$$d_{BL}(\omega,
u):=\sup\left\{\left|\int\phi\,d(\omega-
u)ight|:\|\phi\|_\infty\le1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(\phi)\le1ight\}.$$
The integral bound by total variation shows this supremum is finite. This page uses only the displayed dual quantity and makes no separate metric-separation claim. No Jordan decomposition, positivity, or probability normalization is needed.
def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, with the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. An interaction kernel is a continuous map $K:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$. It is globally Lipschitz with constant $L\ge0$ in the convention used on this page if
$$|K(x,y)-K(x',y')|\le L(|x-x'|+|y-y'|)$$
for all $x,y,x',y'\in\mathbb R^d$. This implies the linear-growth estimate
$$|K(x,y)|\le |K(0,0)|+L(|x|+|y|).$$
The notation $L$ always refers to this two-variable convention; the stability factor below is therefore $2L$.
def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel:
## Definition

In two dimensions let $z^\perp=(-z_2,z_1)$ and
$$G(z)=\frac1{2\pi}\log|z|,\qquad K(z)=\nabla^\perp G(z)=\frac{z^\perp}{2\pi|z|^2}\quad(z\ne0).$$
The locally integrable value assigned to $K(0)$ is immaterial. Fix a radial, nonnegative smooth bump $\rho$ supported in the unit ball with $\int\rho=1$; its scaled family is the mollifier family of [[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]]. Put $\rho_\varepsilon(z)=\varepsilon^{-2}\rho(z/\varepsilon)$, $G_\varepsilon=G*\rho_\varepsilon$, and
$$K_\varepsilon=K*\rho_\varepsilon.$$
The kernel is a regularized interaction; its smoothness and global Lipschitz property are proved in a separate lemma. It does not define the singular physical interaction at a collision.
def-p-one-wasserstein-one:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$. For Borel probability measures $\mu,\nu$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite first moments $\int |x|\,d\mu(x)<\infty$ and $\int |y|\,d\nu(y)<\infty$, let $\Pi(\mu,\nu)$ be the set of Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ whose first and second marginals are $\mu$ and $\nu$. Define
$$W_1(\mu,\nu):=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int_{\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d}|x-y|\,d\pi(x,y).$$
This definition makes no assertion that the infimum is attained. It applies only to probability measures with finite first moment; it is not a distance assigned here to a general signed measure.

Here $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and probability measure has the meaning of [[def-probability-measure]].
def-signed-split-transport-cost:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice when invoking [[thm-jordan-decomposition-for-signed-measures]]. Let $\omega,
u$ be finite signed Borel measures on $\mathbb R^d$ whose total variations have finite first moments. Write their Jordan parts as $\omega^+,\omega^-$ and $
u^+,
u^-$. If the positive-part masses agree and the negative-part masses agree, define
$$C_{\pm}(\omega,
u):=\inf_{\pi^+,\pi^-}\left(\int|x-y|d\pi^+(x,y)+\int|x-y|d\pi^-(x,y)ight),$$
where $\pi^+$ ranges over finite nonnegative couplings of $\omega^+$ and $
u^+$, and $\pi^-$ over finite nonnegative couplings of $\omega^-$ and $
u^-$. The infimum is over both sign couplings independently. This cost is not the probability $W_1$.
lem-weighted-continuous-path-space-is-co:
## Statement

Let $(E,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a probability space, $T>0$, and $d\ge1$. Use the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Let $\mathcal X$ be the space, modulo equality $\mu$-almost everywhere, of jointly measurable maps $X:[0,T]\times E\to\mathbb R^d$ whose paths are continuous for almost every label and whose time-supremum function is measurable, and for which
$$\|X\|_{\mathcal X}:=\int_E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t(z)|d\mu(z)<\infty.$$
The seminorm identifies maps equal almost everywhere, and the induced distance $d_{\mathcal X}(X,Y)=\|X-Y\|_{\mathcal X}$ is a metric on the quotient; it is complete.
alg-tensor-simpson-force-evaluator:
## Definition

Input a rectangle $R=[a,b]\times[c,d]$ with $a<b$, $c<d$, even integers $n_x,n_y\ge2$, and an exact evaluation oracle for $F:R\to\mathbb R^2$. Return status invalid-domain if either interval is degenerate or reversed, and status invalid-panel-count if either panel count is not an even integer at least two. Otherwise set $h_x=(b-a)/n_x$, $h_y=(d-c)/n_y$, apply [[alg-composite-simpson-rule]] componentwise in the $x$ direction and then the $y$ direction, and return the resulting tensor sum $Q_yQ_xF$. If an evaluation oracle reports an unavailable value, stop at the first such grid point and return evaluation-failure with that point. The exact-real procedure makes finitely many evaluations and sums. This definition makes no floating-point roundoff or force-accuracy claim; error control is a separate result.
def-characteristic-mean-field-solution:
## Definition

Fix $T>0$, a globally Lipschitz kernel $K$ as in [[def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel]], and a Borel probability measure $\mu_0$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite first moment as in [[def-p-one-wasserstein-one]]. A characteristic solution on $[0,T]$ consists of a jointly Borel map $X:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$, defined up to a $\mu_0$-null set of labels, such that $t\mapsto X_t(x)$ is absolutely continuous for $\mu_0$-almost every $x$, $X_0(x)=x$, and
$$X_t(x)=x+\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(X_s(x),X_s(y))\,d\mu_0(y)\,ds$$
for $\mu_0$-almost every $x$. It transports $\mu_0$ to $\mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0$, where $(X_t)_\#\mu_0(A):=\mu_0(X_t^{-1}(A))$. The weighted path integrability convention is $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t(x)|d\mu_0(x)<\infty$; in particular every time slice has finite first moment.
def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-parti:
## Definition

For a globally Lipschitz interaction kernel $K$ and $N\ge1$, the equal-probability mean-field particle system is
$$\dot x_i(t)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N K(x_i(t),x_j(t)),\qquad i=1,\ldots,N.$$
Its empirical probability measure is $\mu_N(t)=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i(t)}$.

For a mollified two-dimensional Biot-Savart kernel $K_\varepsilon$ from [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]] and real weights $\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_N$, the weighted signed vortex particle system is
$$\dot x_i(t)=\sum_{j=1}^N\Gamma_jK_\varepsilon(x_i(t)-x_j(t)),\qquad i=1,\ldots,N,$$
with vorticity measure $\omega_N(t)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i(t)}$. If $\Gamma_i=1/N$ and $K(x,y)=K_\varepsilon(x-y)$, the first system is the probability special case. The weighted signed system is a first-order Biot-Savart model.
def-signed-vorticity-characteristic-solu:
## Definition

Assume AC. Let $\omega_0$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb R^2$, set $M=|\omega_0|(\mathbb R^2)$, and let $\omega_0=\omega_0^+-\omega_0^-$ be its Jordan decomposition. If $M=0$, its characteristic solution is the constant zero measure curve. If $M>0$, set $E=\mathbb R^2\times\{+1,-1\}$ and define the probability measure $\lambda_0$ by $\lambda_0(A\times\{s\})=\omega_0^s(A)/M$ for Borel $A$ and $s\in\{+1,-1\}$. A signed characteristic solution for the regularized kernel $K_\varepsilon$ on $[0,T]$ is a jointly measurable path map $Z:[0,T]\times E\to\mathbb R^2$, modulo $\lambda_0$-almost everywhere equality, with absolutely continuous paths for almost every label, $Z_0(x,s)=x$, and

$$Z_t(x,s)=x+M\int_0^t\int_E rK_\varepsilon(Z_u(x,s)-Z_u(y,r))\,d\lambda_0(y,r)\,du,$$

such that its time-supremum function is measurable and $\int_E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|Z_t(x,s)|\,d\lambda_0(x,s)<\infty$. It represents the signed measure curve

$$\omega_t=M\int_E s\,\delta_{Z_t(x,s)}\,d\lambda_0(x,s).$$

Here $\omega_0^s$ denotes $\omega_0^+$ when $s=+1$ and $\omega_0^-$ when $s=-1$. The total variation mass is $M$ at time zero, and the sign coordinate records each Jordan part separately.
lem-mollified-biot-savart-kernel-is-smoo:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the mollifier of [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. For every $\varepsilon>0$, $G_\varepsilon$ and $K_\varepsilon$ are $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^2$, and there is $C_\rho<\infty$ independent of $\varepsilon$ such that
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^2}\|DK_\varepsilon(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_\rho\varepsilon^{-2}.$$
Consequently $K_\varepsilon$ is globally Lipschitz with constant at most $C_\rho\varepsilon^{-2}$.
lem-signed-bl-norm-dominated-by-split-co:
## Statement

Assume AC for the Jordan decompositions in [[def-signed-split-transport-cost]]. If finite signed measures $\omega,
u$ have the same positive-part mass and the same negative-part mass, and their total variations have finite first moments, then the couplings in $C_{\pm}(\omega,
u)$ exist, $C_{\pm}(\omega,
u)<\infty$, and
$$d_{BL}(\omega,
u)\le C_{\pm}(\omega,
u).$$
lem-w1-is-finite-on-probability-measures:
## Statement

If $\mu,
u$ are Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite first moments, then $\Pi(\mu,
u)$ is nonempty and $W_1(\mu,
u)<\infty$ for the definition in [[def-p-one-wasserstein-one]].
def-separable-regularized-vortex-interac:
## Definition

For $N\ge2$, real weights $\Gamma_i$, and $\varepsilon>0$, define the open collision-free configuration set $Q_{cf}:=\{q=(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in(\mathbb R^2)^N:q_i\ne q_j\text{ for }i\ne j\}$. Let $q\in Q_{cf}$ and $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_N)\in(\mathbb R^2)^N$. Let
$$H_\varepsilon(q,p)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^N|p_i|^2+V_\varepsilon(q),\qquad V_\varepsilon(q)=\sum_{i<j}\Gamma_i\Gamma_jG_\varepsilon(q_i-q_j),$$
where $G_\varepsilon$ is from [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. This is a separable canonical Hamiltonian on $Q_{cf}$; its local leapfrog map is the partial composition [[def-leapfrog-step-map]] restricted as in [[def-local-leapfrog-domain-on-an-open-configuration-set]]. It is a distinct second-order canonical comparison model, not the first-order Biot-Savart vortex system of [[def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-particle-systems]].
thm-dobrushin-w1-stability-for-character:
## Statement

Let $K$ have two-variable Lipschitz constant $L$ as in [[def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel]], and let $\mu_t,\nu_t$ be characteristic solutions from probability measures with finite first moments. For every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$W_1(\mu_t,\nu_t)\le e^{2Lt}W_1(\mu_0,\nu_0).$$
The estimate is proved for every prescribed initial coupling before taking the infimum; existence of an optimal coupling is not assumed.
thm-empirical-measures-solve-mean-field-:
## Statement

Let $x_1,\ldots,x_N$ solve the equal-probability system of [[def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-particle-systems]] on $[0,T]$, and put $\mu_N(t)=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i(t)}$. Then for every $\varphi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^d)$,
$$\int\varphi d\mu_N(t)-\int\varphi d\mu_N(0) =\int_0^t\int\nabla\varphi(x)\cdot\left(\int K(x,y)d\mu_N(s)(y)\right)d\mu_N(s)(x)ds.$$
Thus the empirical measure satisfies the same weak transport equation exactly, with no particle quadrature error in this identity.
thm-mean-field-characteristic-flow-exist:
## Statement

Let $K$ be globally Lipschitz with constant $L$ in the convention of [[def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel]], and let $\mu_0$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite first moment. For every finite $T>0$ there exists a characteristic solution on $[0,T]$ in the sense of [[def-characteristic-mean-field-solution]]. It is unique up to equality of trajectories for $\mu_0$-almost every label. No compact support assumption is needed.
thm-mean-field-characteristics-satisfy-w:
## Statement

Let $\mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0$ be the characteristic solution for a globally Lipschitz kernel on $[0,T]$. For every $\varphi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^d)$ and $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\int\varphi\,d\mu_t-\int\varphi\,d\mu_0 =\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R^d}\nabla\varphi(x)\cdot\left(\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(x,y)d\mu_s(y)\right)d\mu_s(x)ds.$$
thm-mollified-biot-savart-kernel-has-l1-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the radial compactly supported mollifier of [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. Write $\|F\|_{L^1}:=\int_{\mathbb R^2}|F(x)|dx$ and let $\|g\|_{L^\infty}$ be the essential supremum of $|g|$. There is a constant $C_\rho<\infty$, independent of $\varepsilon>0$, such that
$$\|K_\varepsilon-K\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^2)}\le C_\rho\varepsilon.$$
Consequently, for every bounded measurable vorticity density $\omega$,
$$\|(K_\varepsilon-K)*\omega\|_{L^\infty}\le C_\rho\varepsilon\|\omega\|_{L^\infty}.$$
This is an error estimate at fixed $\varepsilon$; it does not prove a singular-limit theorem for the particle dynamics.
thm-signed-dobrushin-stability-with-forc:

u_0$ have separately matching positive and negative Jordan masses and total variation mass $M$. For $M>0$, use the Jordan-label probability spaces of [[def-signed-vorticity-characteristic-solution]] and suppose their path maps $X^\omega_t(x,s)$ and $X^
u_t(y,s)$ have integrable time suprema, satisfy $X^\omega_0(x,s)=x$ and $X^

Suppose their absolutely continuous sign-labelled trajectories satisfy

for almost every time and almost every label of sign $s\in\{+,-\}$, with $|r_\omega|\le\eta_\omega$ and $|r_

u$ on $[0,T]$. For every prescribed initial pair of sign-preserving couplings of total cost $D_0$,

If $M=0$, both curves are zero and the inequalities hold with zero right side. Taking the infimum over initial couplings in the $M>0$ case gives the same bound with $D_0=C_{\pm}(\omega_0,

thm-signed-regularized-vorticity-charact:
## Statement

Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $\omega_0$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb R^2$ whose total variation has finite first moment, and let $K_\varepsilon$ be the smooth mollified Biot-Savart kernel of [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. There is a unique signed characteristic solution in the sense of [[def-signed-vorticity-characteristic-solution]] on every finite interval $[0,T]$, and it represents the measure curve with velocity
$$u_t(x)=\int K_\varepsilon(x-y)d\omega_t(y),\qquad \omega_t=(X_t)_\#\omega_0.$$
The flow is a homeomorphism of $\mathbb R^2$ at each time and
$$|\omega_t|(\mathbb R^2)=|\omega_0|(\mathbb R^2).$$
If $\omega_0=0$, the only transported measure curve is identically zero.
thm-w1-dobrushin-stability-with-force-de:
## Statement

Let $K$ have two-variable global Lipschitz constant $L$ as in [[def-globally-lipschitz-mean-field-kernel]]. Let $\mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0$ and $
u_t=(Y_t)_\#
u_0$ be probability curves from finite-first-moment initial laws, with absolutely continuous characteristic paths satisfying
$$\dot X_t(x)=\int K(X_t(x),X_t(z))d\mu_0(z)+r_\mu(t,x),\qquad \dot Y_t(y)=\int K(Y_t(y),Y_t(w))d
u_0(w)+r_
u(t,y)$$
for almost every time and almost every label, with $X_0(x)=x$ and $Y_0(y)=y$. Assume additionally the weighted path integrability conditions $\int\sup_{s\le T}|X_s|d\mu_0<\infty$ and $\int\sup_{s\le T}|Y_s|d
u_0<\infty$. Assume the measurable label defects satisfy $|r_\mu|\le\eta_\mu$ and $|r_
u|\le\eta_
u$ on $[0,T]$. For every prescribed initial coupling $\pi_0$ of cost $D_0$, its transport by the two characteristic paths has cost at time $t$ at most
$$e^{2Lt} igl(D_0+(\eta_\mu+\eta_
u)t igr).$$
Consequently $W_1(\mu_t,
u_t)\le e^{2Lt} igl(W_1(\mu_0,
u_0)+(\eta_\mu+\eta_
u)t igr)$. The estimate is first proved for each coupling; no optimal plan is assumed.
thm-weighted-signed-vortex-particles-sat:
## Statement

Let $x_i:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^2$ be $C^1$ trajectories with fixed real weights $\Gamma_i$, and let $g:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be a common continuous force correction. Suppose
$$\dot x_i(t)=\sum_{j=1}^N\Gamma_jK_\varepsilon(x_i(t)-x_j(t))+g(t,x_i(t)),$$
where $K_\varepsilon$ is the mollified kernel in [[def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-particle-systems]]. For $\omega_N(t)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i(t)}$ and every $\varphi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^2)$,
$$\int\varphi d\omega_N(t)-\int\varphi d\omega_N(0) =\int_0^t\int\nabla\varphi(x)\cdot\left(\int K_\varepsilon(x-y)d\omega_N(s)(y)+g(s,x)\right)d\omega_N(s)(x)ds.$$
In particular, the uncorrected regularized particle system satisfies the same weak identity with $g=0$.
lem-classical-rk4-map-is-lipschitz-on-a-:
## Statement

Let $f:[0,T]\times U\to\mathbb R^m$ be uniformly $L$-Lipschitz in its state variable on a set containing every stage generated by the classical RK4 step of [[def-euler-midpoint-rk4-tableaus]] from any two admitted starting states $u,v$ at the same base time $t$. Assume all these stage evaluations are defined, and let $\Psi_h(t,\cdot)$ be the resulting one-step map for $0<h\le h_0$. Then
$$|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)|\le(1+L_*h)|u-v|,\qquad L_*=Le^{Lh_0}.$$
thm-separable-vortex-inspired-leapfrog-i:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $H_\varepsilon(q,p)=\frac12|p|^2+V_\varepsilon(q)$ be the separable Hamiltonian of [[def-separable-regularized-vortex-interaction-hamiltonian]]. On an open collision-free configuration set, restrict the leapfrog step to states whose kick and drift stages remain in that set, as in [[def-local-leapfrog-domain-on-an-open-configuration-set]]. Then every admitted step has the following properties:

1. it is reversible: its inverse on its image is the admitted step with signed step size $-h$;
2. it is symplectic on its open admitted domain;
3. it preserves local phase volume, meaning Lebesgue measure of every measurable set and its image agree; and
4. for a fixed $T>0$ and integer $N\ge1$, with $h=T/N>0$ sufficiently small, if $V_\varepsilon\in C^3$ and the exact path, numerical states, and every kick/drift stage lie in a common compact convex tube $K\Subset Q_{cf}\times(\mathbb R^2)^N$ with derivatives of the Hamiltonian vector field through order two bounded there, the global trajectory error is $O(h^2)$ on $[0,T]$.

Claims 1–3 concern every signed admitted step; claim 4 has the stated positive-step tube hypotheses. The symplecticity and order-two conclusions use the exact hypotheses of the suppliers [[prop-local-leapfrog-and-symplectic-euler-are-symplectic]] and [[thm-local-symplectic-euler-and-leapfrog-trajectory-errors]]. This canonical second-order Hamiltonian is a comparison model; it is not the first-order Biot-Savart particle system.
thm-tensor-simpson-force-error:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, $c<d$, let $n_x,n_y\ge2$ be even integers, and set $R=[a,b]\times[c,d]$, $h_x=(b-a)/n_x$, $h_y=(d-c)/n_y$. If $F\in C^4(R,\mathbb R^2)$ and
$$M_{40}=\max_R|\partial_x^4F|,\qquad M_{04}=\max_R|\partial_y^4F|,$$
then the tensor evaluator of [[alg-tensor-simpson-force-evaluator]] satisfies
$$\left|\int_R F-Q_yQ_xF\right|\le\frac{\sqrt2\,|R|}{180}\bigl(h_x^4M_{40}+h_y^4M_{04}\bigr),\qquad |R|=(b-a)(d-c).$$
This is an exact-arithmetic quadrature bound, not a roundoff estimate.
thm-rk4-global-error-for-regularized-vor:
## Statement

Fix $\varepsilon>0$, finitely many vortex weights, $T>0$, and the regularized finite-particle vector field of [[def-mean-field-and-weighted-vortex-particle-systems]], possibly with an added common smooth force correction $g_q(t,X,x_i)$ for spatial force quadrature. Suppose the resulting nonautonomous state field $f(t,X)$ is jointly $C^4$ on an open time-state domain, with derivatives through order four bounded on a common compact convex tube $\mathcal T$ compactly contained in that domain. Assume the exact path, RK4 grid states, and every RK4 stage lie in that tube for $h=T/N\le h_0$, and the common force correction is included in these bounds. Let $C_4$ be a uniform exact-start defect constant, so the local defect is at most $C_4h^5$ as in [[def-one-step-ode-method-local-defect-order-and-stability]]. Let $L_*h$ be the stability coefficient from [[lem-classical-rk4-map-is-lipschitz-on-a-controlled-tube]]. For exact initialization, the state errors $E_k$ satisfy
$$\max_{0\le k\le N}E_k\le \begin{cases} C_4\dfrac{e^{L_*T}-1}{L_*}h^4,&L_*>0,\\ C_4Th^4,&L_*=0. \end{cases}$$
The tube and stage-admissibility assumptions are conditional; no invariance or global numerical-domain claim is made. The constant $C_4$ may depend on $\varepsilon$, particle count, the quadrature field, and the tube.
thm-mean-field-vortex-blob-error-budget:
## Statement

Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $\omega_t$ be a smooth finite signed vorticity density on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^2$ with finite first moment, transported by a sign-preserving characteristic flow $X_t$ satisfying $\omega_t=(X_t)_\#\omega_0$ and $\dot X_t(x)=(K*\omega_t)(X_t(x))$, where $K$ is the singular kernel in [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. Assume $\sup_{t\le T}\|\omega_t\|_\infty\le W$, $\int\sup_{t\le T}|X_t(x)|d|\omega_0|(x)<\infty$, and the flow transports each Jordan part to the corresponding Jordan part. Put $M=|\omega_0|(\mathbb R^2)$. Let
$$\omega_N^0=\sum_{i=1}^N\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^0}$$
be a finite signed particle measure whose positive and negative Jordan masses respectively equal those of $\omega_0$, with finite first moment, and with consolidated atoms whose positive and negative supports are disjoint; thus $\sum_i|\Gamma_i|=M$. Let $E_0=C_{\pm}(\omega_0,\omega_N^0)<\infty$.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$. For every time and force location $(t,x)$, suppose the force integrand $F_{t,x}:R\to\mathbb R^2$ lies in $C^4(R,\mathbb R^2)$ and its fourth partial derivatives satisfy the uniform bounds $M_{40},M_{04}$. Let the tensor Simpson evaluator use the even panel counts and widths in [[thm-tensor-simpson-force-error]], and define its residual by $r_q(t,x)=Q_yQ_xF_{t,x}-\int_R F_{t,x}$. Thus
$$\eta_q=\frac{\sqrt2|R|}{180}(h_x^4M_{40}+h_y^4M_{04}).$$
Assume this residual is the same correction function for every particle, $\sup_{t,x}|r_q(t,x)|\le\eta_q$, and the corrected regularized particle flow preserves the two Jordan parts. Write $x_i^{\varepsilon,q}$ for the exact solution from $x_i^0$ of
$$\dot x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)=\sum_{j=1}^N\Gamma_jK_\varepsilon(x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)-x_j^{\varepsilon,q}(t))+r_q(t,x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)),$$
and set $\omega_N^{\varepsilon,q}(t)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)}$. Assume $r_q$ and the resulting finite-dimensional particle field are jointly $C^4$ in time and state with derivatives through order four bounded on a compact tube containing all exact paths and RK4 stages. Let $x_i^h(T)$ be the RK4 states from the same initial data for this ODE, and define $\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^h(T)}$. Let $h=T/n\le h_0$ for an integer $n\ge1$ and define $C_{RK}:=C_4(e^{L_*T}-1)/L_*$ if $L_*>0$, and $C_{RK}:=C_4T$ if $L_*=0$, where $C_4,L_*,h_0$ are the constants in [[thm-rk4-global-error-for-regularized-vortex-particles]]. Then
$$d_{BL}(\omega_T,\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T)) \le e^{2L_\varepsilon MT}\left(E_0+MT\left(C_\rho\varepsilon W+\eta_q\right)\right)+MC_{RK}h^4,$$
where $L_\varepsilon$ is a one-variable global Lipschitz constant for $K_\varepsilon$; the induced two-variable constant for $K_\varepsilon(x-y)$ is also $L_\varepsilon$. The terms are initial signed particle approximation, blob regularization, force quadrature, and RK4 time error. The constants may depend on $\varepsilon$, particle count, and the tube; no uniform singular limit as $\varepsilon\to0$ is claimed.
